Package edu.bu.pas.hex.agents

Class ATPZSMCTSAgent<T extends ATPZSNode>

java.lang.Object
edu.bu.pas.hex.agents.ATPZSTreeSearchAgent<T>
edu.bu.pas.hex.agents.ATPZSMCTSAgent<T>
All Implemented Interfaces:
Agent, TreeSearcher
public abstract class ATPZSMCTSAgent<T extends ATPZSNode> extends ATPZSTreeSearchAgent<T>
Represents an Agent that chooses Actions using a Monte-Carlo Tree-Search (MCTS) algorithm in an alternating two-player zero-sum setting. The MCTS algorithm repeats the following four steps to grow a game tree until resources are exhausted.
  1. Choose an artificial leaf node in the game tree. This process happens by walking from the root of the game tree until an artificial leaf node is encountered. Note that an artificial leaf node in this case could be a nonterminal with no children *or* it could be a nonterminal where not all of its children have been expanded yet.
  2. Once an artificial leaf node has been chosen, choose an action available in that artificial leaf node and get the child node. In order to be considered an artificial leaf node, there exists at least one child of this node that has yet to be expanded. You must choose one unexpanded child and visit it: expanding the game tree.
  3. Once a new child has been expanded, you need to collect a utility sample of an outcome possible from playing the game to completion from this node. If this node is terminal, you can ask your utility function. If this node is a nonterminal, you have to perform a rollout to sample a branch where this node is the root.
  4. Once you have a sample of this outcome utility, you need to backup this sample for all q-values in the path from the root of the tree to the child you just expanded. If the child is a terminal you can set the terminalUtility attribute of the ATPZSNode otherwise you need to update the corresponding q-value.

Note that there are many *flavors* of MCTS, so a child class must implement the four abstract methods introduced in this type in order to specify *which* flavor of MCTS the child is using.

  • Method Details

    • selectArtificialLeaf

      public abstract T selectArtificialLeaf(T rootNode)
      The first step of an MCTS algorithm. Walk the tree until you arrive at an artificial leaf node. Remember that an artificial leaf node is defined here as a nonterminal who has at least one Action that can be taken but has not been explored yet.
      Parameters:
      rootNode - the root of the tree.
      Returns:
      An artificial leaf node.

    • chooseChild

      public abstract T chooseChild(T artificialLeafNode)
      The second step of an MCTS algorithm. Once an artificial leaf has been chosen you need to pick one of its unexplored Actions (which is the same as choosing one of its child ATPZSNodes). This child should be added into the game tree. Remember that you need to call the addChild method on a ATPZSNode object in order for a ATPZSNode to cache that child.
      Parameters:
      artificialLeafNode - The artificial leaf node chosen from step 1.
      Returns:
      The new ATPZSNode child node. This child should have already been added to the tree.

    • getRolloutOutcome

      public abstract double getRolloutOutcome(T leafNode)
      The third step of an MCTS algorithm. Once a new child has been chosen, you need to perform a rollout to get a sample of the utility an outcome possible from playing the game from the child can be. If the child is terminal, you can ask your utility function. If it a nonterminal then you need to perform a rollout: play the game until completion from the child.

      Remember that you cannot invoke your opponent when playing the rest of the rollout, nor should you invoke your own Agent's logic during this process. Rollouts need to be fast, so if you were to perform tree search during the rollout it would defeat the point. I recommend that you use "proxy agents" to stand in for the Agents playing the game. For instance you are welcome to make edu.bu.pas.hex.agents.RandomAgent instances and use them to play the rest of the game. To do so you would need to create a new Game instance from the child game, set the Agents for both teams, and then play that game until completion with something like the following: 

      
 Agent agentA = new RandomAgent(maxThinkingTimeMs);
 Agent agentB = new RandomAgent(maxThinkingTimeMs);
 GenericGame game = childGameView.getMutableInstance(agentA, agentB).playUntilCompletion();
 Double myUtility = game.getOutcomeUtility(myPlayerIdx); // will be 'null' if the game is not terminal
      Parameters:
      leafNode - the new child to get a sample of an outcome's utility of.
      Returns:
      the utility value of the rollout's outcome.

    • backupStatistics

      public abstract void backupStatistics(T leafNode, double rolloutOutcomeUtility)
      The fourth step of an MCTS algorithm. Once you have the rollout utility, you need to walk the path from the leafnode back to the root of the game tree updating statistics along the way (e.g. updating the statistics of each node along the way).
      Parameters:
      leafNode - the leaf the rollout was performed on. Each ATPZSNode has a parent inside it.
      rolloutOutcomeUtility - The utility value of the rollout's outcome from step 3.
